subject: Biology
central_question: How do green plants capture light energy and use it to make carbohydrates from carbon dioxide and water while releasing oxygen?
in_scope_units: Prior evidence that chlorophyll, light and carbon dioxide are required for photosynthesis.
Early experiments by Priestley, Ingenhousz, Sachs, Engelmann and van Niel.
Chloroplast organisation and the locations of light and carbon reactions.
Photosynthetic pigments, absorption spectra and action spectra.
Light reactions, photosystems, electron transport and splitting of water.
Cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation and chemiosmotic ATP synthesis.
Use of ATP and NADPH in the Calvin cycle.
C4 pathway, Kranz anatomy and photorespiration.
Internal and external factors affecting photosynthesis.

known_pitfalls.claim: The oxygen released in photosynthesis comes from carbon dioxide.
known_pitfalls.correction: The oxygen released by green plants comes from water splitting.

known_pitfalls.claim: Dark reactions occur only in darkness.
known_pitfalls.correction: They are not directly light driven, but they depend on ATP and NADPH produced by light reactions.

known_pitfalls.claim: C4 plants do not use the Calvin cycle.
known_pitfalls.correction: C4 plants concentrate CO2 first, then run the Calvin cycle in bundle-sheath cells.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Exercise 5 to explain why chlorophyll a cannot be replaced by chlorophyll b.
Use NCERT Exercise 9(b) to compare cyclic and non-cyclic photophosphorylation.
Use the in-text Calvin-cycle balance to calculate ATP and NADPH per glucose.
Use NCERT Exercise 8 and Figure 11.10 to interpret limiting factors.
Use NCERT Exercise 4 to explain why C4 RuBisCO performs more carboxylation.
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The end-of-chapter EXERCISES section contains Questions 1-9 on C3 and C4 plants, pigments, RuBisCO, light limitation and pathway comparisons.
